Offline Qiling developer harness; no HTTP route or live account flow. Defaults to public ARM64 hello. decoder-init uses own-source asset/log/JNI adapters; unsupported asset/JNI operations abort. Both extraction checks require an existing empty decoded directory and preserve partial outputs. The partial-range result is native 9/2, AssetDecompressionException and exit 7; full extraction under Qiling remains unverified after bounded timeouts and cancellation of a slower run when the separate QEMU runner succeeded. A parent subprocess enforces the wall limit (default 10 seconds); ARM64 basic blocks are conservatively charged across guest threads before execution (default 1000000 instructions). Qiling threaded run timeout/count alone were refuted as bounds. host-meminfo maps real host /proc/meminfo for local resource estimation. Empty guest environment; missing fixtures/dependencies and invalid bounds fail preflight. Proc-exe stat uses actual fixture metadata; munmap permits valid wholly unmapped ranges, rejects unaligned/zero-length input and delegates mapped ranges. trace-worker requires an extraction check and the exact 37.71 ARM64 decoder SHA-256; unknown layouts fail preflight. It reports at most 64 exceptional stage/offset, stream/type, declared/requested/produced counts and hash_check records. Pinned partial-range tracing shows stream 6 produced/declared=125448, requested=0, hash_check=0 and the oversized-file branch. Read-only futex observation reports up to 64 transitions as thread/local selector/op/val/timeout_present, collapsing consecutive duplicates without addresses. Instruction progress prints every 100 million charged. Maximum 600 seconds/10 billion instructions are local tooling budgets, not server limits. No native safety-number algorithm or Android application compatibility is established. Evidence and setup: docs/protocol/native-unpacking.md and tools/apk-research/README.md.

Offline fast comparison of already exported checksum-verified bundles; reads no APK/account/network and mutates nothing. JSON reports old_apk/new_apk hashes and topic entries: topic, status (added/removed/changed/unchanged), old_file/new_file, old_class/new_class, rust_files (union of mapped paths). Validates bounded listed-file contents/checksums and rejects unsafe filenames/tampering. Ignores only the per-file APK hash header when comparing topic bodies; class names, offsets, instructions and unresolved opcode markers remain significant. Structural changes do not automatically establish changed protocol semantics; obfuscation must be re-anchored in a new hash-pinned recipe. Unmapped/native code is explicitly outside comparison scope. artifacts lists non-topic metadata/dictionary files with file, status and old_file/new_file; changed manifest/inventory/targets/tokens remain visible. Offline anchor-assisted class/method relocation. Scans all configured exact string anchors in one checked APK DEX traversal, aborting DEX/read/structural errors instead of accepting partial warning-only results. DEX-local method indices distinguish overloaded names/shorties and repeated loads in one method deduplicate. Anchors must share one physical method for method-scoped targets, or one physical class for whole-class targets; missing or split strings do not cause fallback to old selectors. JSON reports previous_apk/candidate_apk, all_unique, topics with topic/status (unique/missing/ambiguous/unanchored/no_common_scope), previous_class/previous_method, scope, candidates, anchor_sites and rust_files. Each site/candidate has dex_file, class_name, method_name, method_proto (shorty), method_index (APK-local) and dex_byte_off. Candidates carry a representative site; anchor_sites retains every occurrence. --output writes a new SHA-256-pinned proposal only when every target is unique and never overwrites a file; a requested unresolved proposal exits nonzero after printing the report. Whole-class scope retains method=null; method targets adopt the observed name. This is structural location, not semantic equivalence, complete DEX verification, native mapping or automatic Rust patching. Original recipe/account/files remain untouched. Public source APK evidence only, no HTTP route/network/account access. Optional caller_anchors requires all caller strings in one physical method that symbolically invokes the candidate. Exact declaring class/name/full parameter-and-return descriptors match across DEX method tables, distinguishing overloads with identical shorties. Checked caller scans fail reported errors without partial warning-only output. Added statuses are missing_caller_anchor, no_common_caller_scope and no_matching_caller. Configured topics additionally report initial_candidates, caller_anchors, caller_anchor_sites, qualifying_callers, caller_matches (target/signature/callers); candidates is the filtered set. Empty/noninvoking caller evidence never falls back to the previous selector. No reflective/native/virtual-dispatch reachability claim, semantic patching, HTTP route or account access. Recipe method targets additionally accept exact method_shorty (1..256 DEX shorty characters; V return-only), requiring a method filter. Export and remap enforce the same constraint. Remap preserves before_shorty_candidates and diagnoses no_matching_shorty without name fallback; shorties are not full signatures. APK 37.71 subject time diagnostics match three methods, JLL selects the long parser; two string-free helper topics remain automatically unresolved. Recipe root include_exception_tables (boolean, default false) is preserved in a resolved proposal; it changes bundle catch-table rendering, not relocation scope or semantic equivalence.

Offline checked DEX token-array extraction; no HTTP route. Requires a unique decoded initializer and complete typed indexed writes; malformed, ambiguous or unsupported input refuses rather than falling back to raw-byte scanning. APK 37.71 1Rl.<clinit> yields 236 single and four 256-entry double pages. Four historical comparison slots were extraction errors. The comparison codec now uses this Derived fixture; the historical 37.70 fixture and pinned Android profile remain preserved. Existing captured projections and account reservations are not replayed or reset. Corrected literal wire-byte regression tests pass; live acceptance of individual corrected tokens remains unverified. Evidence: docs/protocol/token-extraction.md.

Offline selected MEX persisted-ID extractor; no HTTP route or account access. Default namespace whatsapp-android-mex. Reads exact assets/<namespace>_client_persist_ids.json, refuses missing/duplicate ZIP names and over-budget input, exports at most 64 exact operation names to sorted JSON with format_version=1, apk_version, apk_sha256, namespace, asset_path, asset_sha256 and operations. Each operation records operation_name, operation_name_hash, operation_text_hash, client_doc_id, exact decimal-string server doc_id and schema. Positive u64 extraction avoids floating-point rounding. Unknown extra source fields require separate review. APK 2.26.37.71 selected QueryGroupInfo fixture established; complete namespace-registration linkage, native branches and next-release compatibility remain unverified. Evidence docs/protocol/mex.md.

Offline Rust QueryGroupInfo request preview, no HTTP route, account/store access, ID allocation, queued action or live request. Uses explicit server doc_id from selected release export, never client_doc_id; emits offline_only, supplied apk_version/apk_sha256 provenance, operation and node with tag, ordered attributes (name/value text or jid), nested children and text content. The supplied provenance is not independently authenticated by preview; run apk-mex-queries --check against the APK. Default context INTERACTIVE; twelve exact source contexts accepted: INTERACTIVE, LID_MIGRATION, NEW_SUBJECT, ACK_GROUP_MISMATCH, SEND_FAILURE, SUB_GROUP_CONFLICT_RECOVERY, INVITE_CODE, PHASH, PARTICIPANT_CHANGE_RECOVERY, PRE_FETCH, UNKNOWN, MISSING_PARTICIPANT_IDENTIFICATION. Preview includes supplied JID and ID; use synthetic diagnostics. Offline APK 37.71 MEX JSON response inspection; no HTTP route, account access, action settlement or group-state application. Wraps the private file in a result (default) or update child and invokes the actual Rust node parser. Local input bound 1 MiB. LaT first-character JSON gate preserved: leading whitespace, binary Argo/Pando, missing/nontext child, malformed UTF-8/JSON and excess size refuse with content-free diagnostics. Library prefers result over update. Redacted output fields payload_child, data_state, data_field_count, errors_state, error_count; states missing/null/valid/invalid. Data must be an object and errors an array when nonnull. Missing/null errors yield an empty known array, while invalid errors remain unknown rather than being treated as absent. Fields parse independently and preserve valid data or opaque error elements when the other field has an invalid type. MexJsonResponse data()/errors() expose private content explicitly; Debug and summary() expose only counts/types. No semantic success verdict is produced, and error_count=0 alone does not establish success. Confirmed provider 0x1763 resolves through 00S/1UE/0yN to O4r selector 0; selectors 2/1 choose nullable data and errors. Java exception fallback strings are not fabricated: the Rust inspector reports invalid field state. Complete Android JSON lexical acceptance, per-error schema/ranking, other callback policies, Argo/Pando and group conversion remain unimplemented. Source docs/protocol/mex.md; sixteen synthetic field-type fixtures cover both payload children, not live responses. --group-info adds group_info_disposition: unsupported_parts, missing_model, invalid_error_entry, server_errors, empty_data, invoke_group_callback. This APK 37.71 group-only gate preserves model-before-error-summary ordering on supported shapes: valid data must exist, error entries must be objects, any nonempty valid error array blocks the group success callback even with partial data, and empty data without errors does not invoke it. Nonempty data without errors invokes A04; the separate feature gate/converter can still fail or skip application. Unsupported local field states do not fabricate Java exceptions. Error codes, waits, summaries and complete converter/state application are not implemented by this gate. Confirmed static IWF error fields extensions.error_code, extensions.backoff, extensions.severity, I1H.A06 extensions.is_retryable (explicit default true) and root code/message/path; explicit root-code fallback 417 applies only when extensions object is absent. Rank/Android coercion and backoff duration remain unported; these are source facts, not new server-response output fields. --group-numbers requires --group-info and explicitly reveals private group_numeric_metadata: creation_scaled, subject_creation_scaled, announcement_version, all signed decimal strings preserving i64 precision. Default output remains redacted. Actual library projection requires InvokeGroupCallback and object xwa2_group_query_by_id; no full group validity or state application. Numeric projection follows ADv.A04/A05 -> 8kY.A0B -> 0Gv.A01 default-zero and wrapping times-1000, while ADv.A03/A4m.A08 version stays unscaled. Nullable/nonobject subject gives zero. Signed-decimal strings support ASCII signs and reference BMP digits via UTF-16, reject whitespace/prefix/fraction/exponent/overflow to zero; signed integral JSON is exact, floating/wider-unsigned/bool/null/array/object numeric results zero via inferred optString/parseLong semantics. Independent executed host Java 21.0.12.1+1 oracle covers 479 cases and all 65536 UTF-16 units, 370 digits/37 BMP blocks; not APK/Android execution. Actual Android SDK/Unicode and full JSON lexical parity remain unverified. Library numeric Debug hides values; failures include no raw private content and no partial stdout. No HTTP route, account access, MEX dispatch or snapshot mutation. Evidence docs/protocol/mex.md#numeric-group-projection-into-rust-2026-10-07. --edge-roles requires --group-info and adds group_participant_edge_roles, an ordered list of recognized enum values unrecognized/admin/member/superadmin for JSONObject edges. Missing/null/nonarray edges yields empty; nonobject entries skip; duplicates preserve order. Callback must permit A04 and both query group and participants must be objects; refusal diagnostics contain no private payload and produce no partial stdout even with --group-numbers. LbE.A0A/A09 uses optJSONArray then optJSONObject; 8yl constructor wraps the object. Role is read from edge, not nested participant; all nonstring role values become unrecognized. This field-only projection precedes ADv.A0D phash short-circuit and participant model/typename/JID validation, so it is not member count/map or authorization/state application. Default response inspection stays redacted and does not expose this list. Eighteen synthetic APK-branch fixtures cover both payload children, not live captures. Static class_def evidence confirms BotJid 0hh -> abstract 0ZX -> UserJid; no-method-body lookup did not mean absence. Complete member/JID/alias/feature application remains unfinished; scalar conversion is described below. Evidence docs/protocol/mex.md#participant-model-fields-and-object-edge-projection-2026-10-07. --participant-scalars requires --group-info and explicitly prints private group_participant_scalars: phash_match boolean and edges in object-edge order, each with join_time (positive signed decimal string or null) and group_history_sent (nullable boolean). APK 37.71 LbE.A0G/Ayj.A1R optInt==1 default then optBoolean; ADv.A0D join_time positive optInt -> 1xf.A17 long and present history -> 8kW.A0q. Missing/null history stays null; other unconvertible values become false. Signed integral JSON Numbers narrow low32 bits; floating Numbers and numeric strings parse/truncate/saturate through Double semantics, with invalid/NaN zero. Java string whitespace <=U+0020, decimal/exponent/type suffix, case-sensitive NaN/Infinity and hexadecimal p-exponent supported; hex rounding uses guard/sticky ties-to-even including subnormals. Independent executed pinned AOSP org.json commit de876a01b29230b877c9f408348c38a90ee724a5 with host Temurin21.0.12.1+1 oracle covers 408 cases; complete Android SDK/JSON lexical parity remains unverified. serde_json float_roundtrip fixes observed local 0.99999999999999994 ->1 misrounding; Java correctly remains below1. Debug hides scalar values. Shared callback/group/participants refusals use mex.group.participants, contain no payload and no partial stdout. Default inspection unchanged. This scalar projection still inspects edges when phash_match=true; it does not treat ADv.A0D null as empty, construct/apply a member map, reclassify identities or contact the server. Source/reference/regression docs/protocol/mex.md#participant-scalar-coercion-and-float-rounding-2026-10-07. --participant-members requires --group-info and explicitly reveals private group_participant_map: kind phash_match with members=null, or kind members with an ordered array. Each member has primary/lid/pn address objects (user, canonical server, kind); nullable aliases; role empty/admin/superadmin; positive join_time as a decimal string or null; nullable group_history_sent; nullable display_name. ADv.A0D phash short-circuits without reading edges; missing/null/nonarray edges become an empty map, nonobject edges and missing/nonobject participant models skip. Unknown model hashes skip. The two known Java UTF-16 hashes (bot c745b457, user 2179873b) are dispatched without invented server typename spellings; fixture names are synthetic hash probes. Invalid nullable bot JIDs skip and that branch ignores aliases/display_name. Strict user primary and present LID/PN aliases abort; later duplicate canonical primary keys replace values at first insertion position. Partial maps never reach stdout. LbE.A0E nullable optString supports strings/bools/signed integral JSON numbers for display/model strings. Unported floating/structured string coercions explicitly refuse with mex.participant.string_coercion; this is a local limitation, not an APK field-type requirement. Bot, LID, PN, interop and traced user singletons retain strict type semantics; aliased identities do not merge distinct primary keys. Debug hides identifiers/content. Filtered interop alias and extra string constructor slots remain null in these branches and are not fabricated. This converter does not validate all group feature gates or apply a durable snapshot, settle an action or contact WhatsApp; downstream phash-null handling, complete Android lexical/string formatting/cache parity and actual typename spellings remain unverified. Local member refusals name the offending id/lid/pn/display_name/__typename attribute without its private value.

Offline APK 2.26.37.71 MEX participant role conversion; no HTTP route, account access, live request or participant/state application. Optional --value supplies a nullable server string; omission, empty, unknown and whitespace-padded values resolve to unrecognized. LbE.A0C -> 4R7.A00 uses Locale.US uppercase without trimming and Enum.valueOf, with IllegalArgumentException fallback to 2hu.A05. ADMIN_MEMBER maps to admin, MEMBER to member, SUPERADMIN_MEMBER to superadmin; explicit UNSET_OR_UNRECOGNIZED_ENUM_VALUE maps to unrecognized. Output offline_only=true, role (unrecognized/admin/member/superadmin) and member_role (empty/admin/superadmin) only, never echoes the supplied value. Evidence docs/protocol/mex.md#participant-role-conversion-and-member-map-boundaries-2026-10-07.

Required --value is private input; success prints only offline_only=true and kind (phone, lid, bot, interop, server_zero, server_name, lid_me, status_me), never the supplied or canonical address. Failure has empty stdout and a content-free mex.participant.address diagnostic. Device suffixes, non-user domains and gdpr refuse. Phone/LID/bot constructor ASCII/length/prefix guards and interop last-hyphen/signed Integer.parseInt rules are preserved. info.title: TeleWhatsApp control API
info.description: This document describes every operation of the whatsapp-api library and whatsapp-cli. The x-transport field indicates whether an operation is served by whatsapp-cli serve over HTTP today or invoked through the CLI. The x-cli field gives the exact command. The x-library field names the Rust entry points behind each operation (crate path form); the whatsapp-cli test `openapi_library_symbols_exist` verifies they exist. The x-live field marks operations that contact WhatsApp servers and require explicit authorization via --allow-live-request. The HTTP control plane has no authentication and binds to loopback only.

fresh_sessions.description: Discard the saved Signal session with each recipient device and establish a new one from a fresh prekey bundle, keeping the pinned peer identity (a changed identity is still refused). Applies to both the direct and the group fan-out path. Only legitimate with positive evidence that the peer never received what was encrypted under the old session.

Both are real — `includeSenderKeysInMessage` is a per-send flag in SendE2EMessageJob and SendLiveLocationKeyJob distributes keys entirely out of band.

mark_read.description: During a messaging session (`listen`), send a read receipt for every incoming direct or group message with readable content (Message fields 1, 3, 6, 7, 8, 9, 26 or 66) that decrypts. Sender-key distributions, protocol messages and reactions get none. Each receipt goes through the same durable, once-only queue as `mark-read`. Applies to `listen` and to `lab-transport --receive`. Off by default: the official client marks messages read when a chat is on screen, which this client cannot infer. Applies to eligible authenticated duplicates on redelivery too, including offline recovery; durable read markers prevent repetitions after uncertain writes or ACKs.

identity_changes.description: Incoming remote prekey trust policy for listen and lab receive. pinned refuses changed saved identities. apk_authenticated permits replacement only after nested message authentication, atomically archiving the prior pin/session and emitting IdentityChanged with the inbox commit. It does not establish human verification. Own-device messages remain pinned. Outgoing bundle replacement has a separate opt-in outgoing_identity_changes; uncertain sends never replay.

outgoing_identity_changes.description: Independent outgoing remote directory-bundle policy for the normal comparison outbox. Pinned suspends changed identities. Apk_authenticated requires a valid signed device key received through authenticated Noise, derives a fresh peer session, archives prior pin/session with signed_directory_bundle provenance and emits IdentityChanged atomically with the original send reservation. Own-account identities remain pinned. It is not human verification. Incoming identity_changes does not enable this. Unknown/refused queries and uncertain sends never resume. Repeating the original outbox-send JSON may resolve an identity-suspended intent using its saved reply; no new query or intent ID is created. General listen --send-outbox does not select suspended intents. Suspensions without an observed pin snapshot cannot resume, and stale replies cannot roll a newer current peer pin back.

post.summary: Decrypt captured direct replies locally, without network I/O
post.description: Decrypt authenticated incoming records locally. The operation is offline. Saved-payload inspection labels Message field 102 as message-history-notice and shows only its nested field numbers, grounded in APK 2.26.37.71 BZc/BV6.dynamicMethod. Supported history-notice metadata is validated using BX5 and DA8.CF4: history receivers, positive oldest-window timestamp and positive message count are required. Diagnostics print metadata=validated with receiver/non-receiver counts and optional-body presence flags, or metadata=unsupported with a fixed redacted reason. They do not print receiver addresses, message counts, timestamp values, context contents or bot metadata. Unknown fields/wire types and duplicate singletons are refused locally. The supported receiver subset is primary numeric PN/LID; other UserJid kinds remain unsupported locally. Local diagnostic limits are 65536 bytes and 1024 entries per receiver list, not server requirements. Context and bot bodies are opaque and not validated. This metadata check does not implement group/app-data dispatch, authorization or rendering. Metadata values remain redacted; history is not fetched or applied. Poll inspection reports question/option byte lengths and counts, selectable count and secret-presence; it no longer prints question or option text. Unknown nested fields remain visible, and malformed nested protobuf fails inspection. This label does not establish sender authorization, history availability, or synchronization completion. With `inspect: true`, display the plaintext protobuf structure without advancing sessions. With replay_captures, preserved message captures are re-run through inbox::process offline to recover stanzas that an earlier defect refused; this is how the first live group messages were recovered after the sender-key distribution field number was corrected. With --inspect, prekey_pin_matches compares the first pkmsg public identity to saved comparison-direct pins for from, sender_pn, participant and participant_pn aliases. Some(true) means matching, Some(false) means differing, None means no saved pin; invalid_input marks malformed inspection data, and invalid_ciphertext marks a non-byte pkmsg payload. This is offline, read-only, prints no keys or full addresses, does not authenticate the ciphertext and does not authorize a pin replacement. Signal failures report fixed redacted categories rather than underlying address/backend strings. --accept-authenticated-identity-changes requires --replay-captures and conflicts with --inspect. It explicitly selects APK-compatible incoming remote key changes after successful authentication. Previous pins/sessions are archived, an IdentityChanged event is emitted atomically with the inbox/session/prekey commit, and no receipt or network request is sent. Default remains pinned. This is not human verification; no safety-number algorithm is claimed. Group pairwise Signal children from a LID participant select the held LID session; participant_pn identifies a contact alias and does not displace that ratchet. post.summary: One comparison-server connection; optional bounded primary login

When the message JSON carries `group` instead of `to`, the send is a sender-key fan-out: a `w:g2` info query resolves the membership, a `usync devices` query resolves each member's devices, `encrypt` supplies bundles for devices without a session, and one `<message>` carries a per-device `<enc>` distribution inside `<participants>` beside the group `skmsg`. It refuses rather than sending when a member has no device list. After any send the connection is held briefly and whatever the server sends next is preserved, because a recipient that cannot decrypt answers with a `receipt type="retry"` naming the failing device. A `<success>` or `<failure>` login result is preserved too: a `<failure>` carries an `appeal_token` and a refusal cannot be replayed to fetch one again. Receive mode shares listen’s durable once-only decryption-failure retry queue; no repeated count=1 requests after redelivery or uncertain writes. Inspect with receipts (offline). Group pairwise Signal children from a LID participant select the held LID session; participant_pn identifies a contact alias and does not displace that ratchet. A mapped new pkmsg establishes a LID session; msg retains PN fallback when no LID session exists. An unmapped LID may use a held session. Wrong-session correction recovered the remaining original group capture offline in an isolated store, without network requests or changing the original account. When mark_read is enabled, eligible authenticated duplicates recovered offline also enter the once-only read queue on redelivery. The helper checks the saved decrypted readable payload; cleared/consumed rows and protocol-only content are skipped. A write-cut regression verifies uncertain reads are never replayed.

post.summary: Maintain an authenticated comparison connection and process incoming messages
post.description: Establish an authenticated session to the messaging server (x-live). Hold the connection for the requested duration, receive incoming messages, and optionally transmit all eligible queued intents. Authenticated Message field-102 notices in a normal group context with meta/appdata=group_history now emit the distinct group_history_notice control event. Receiver addresses/context/bot contents are omitted from its metadata. It is not a human reply or completed history transfer and does not earn an automatic read receipt. Unknown or category-peer contexts stay opaque; internal APK bypasses and UI feature branches are not enabled. Group messages (enc type=skmsg) are decrypted when a SenderKeyDistributionMessage for the (group, sender) pair has been received in a prior or current direct message; messages without a stored sender key are preserved as Unsupported without acknowledgement. SKDM distribution arrives embedded in pkmsg/msg payloads (WhatsApp Message field 2), either standalone or as a second enc child of the group stanza, and is committed atomically with the inbox row. A decrypted group message is confirmed with a receipt addressed to the group carrying the sender as participant. Status updates (from=status@broadcast) route through the same sender-key path and project into a Broadcast chat with the poster as sender, but are never confirmed with a receipt: the status receipt shape (class=status, type=sender) has an unresolved sts input, so none is sent. Each incoming stanza except keepalive replies is reported on stderr as one redacted `incoming` log line (element, type, chat class, enc types, inbox outcome, confirmed, marked_read); this is the default when RUST_LOG is unset. On Undecryptable incoming messages, queues a retry receipt using the saved Signal registration ID. Both listen and lab receive use one request per chat/participant/message ID, durably reserved before transmission; repeats and uncertain outcomes never reset it. This is a conservative client policy, not an APK retry limit. Missing registration or unsupported routing is logged without ending receive; storage failures propagate. The receipts command inspects outcomes offline. Live 2026-10-06: saved-account login and activation succeeded; one automatic retry received a matching server ACK. Its redelivery still failed decryption, and fresh-message automatic read validation remains pending. Signal failure diagnostics classify missing keys, untrusted identity, bad MAC, duplicate counter and invalid encoding without printing peer addresses or backend details. This does not explain the historical window with no incoming message stanzas. Offline preserved-capture inspection found incoming prekey identities differing from both saved PN and LID pins; no pin was replaced. Human safety-number verification is not implemented, and the underlying cause of the saved mismatch remains unknown. Explicit authenticated incoming replacement is available as described below. Direct and group pairwise prekey processing persists first-seen differing public-key fingerprints; identity-conflicts inspects these unauthenticated observations offline. Pins and sessions are not replaced. A failing direct Signal child within a group stanza is also Undecryptable and eligible for the same once-only retry; missing sender-key/session support remains Unsupported. transport.identity_changes explicitly selects pinned (default) or apk_authenticated; the latter atomically archives old remote keys/sessions and emits IdentityChanged after message authentication. Local/own-device identities are not replaced. Group pairwise Signal children from a LID participant select the held LID session; participant_pn identifies a contact alias and does not displace that ratchet. A mapped new pkmsg establishes a LID session; msg retains PN fallback when no LID session exists. An unmapped LID may use a held session. Wrong-session correction recovered the remaining original group capture offline in an isolated store, without network requests or changing the original account. When mark_read is enabled, eligible authenticated duplicates recovered offline also enter the once-only read queue on redelivery. The helper checks the saved decrypted readable payload; cleared/consumed rows and protocol-only content are skipped. A write-cut regression verifies uncertain reads are never replayed. Live 2026-10-07: a 45-second session delivery-confirmed the two recovered direct/group messages as duplicates. A subsequent 20-second session server-acknowledged both explicitly queued saved-message reads; eight reads and one retry are now acknowledged. Handset blue ticks and fresh-message automatic reads remain unconfirmed. Newly settled supported group-action replies now project snapshots/events inside the receive session without requiring group list. Settlement creates a durable pending-projection marker; startup recovers only these newly marked replies and never requeues their requests. Projection and pending-marker removal share the once-only snapshot/event transaction. Truncated or invalid group replies remain encrypted/pending with a secret-free warning and do not stop unrelated receiving; storage errors still stop the session. Group list keeps historical ingestion and its explicit invalid-reply diagnostics. Injected-link and encrypted-store reopen/rollback tests passed. One bounded 30-second authenticated listen session also settled a new info action ok, saved a four-member snapshot during receiving, and left zero projection work for subsequent group list; no chat outbox sends occurred and the previously unresolved two-factor action stayed sent. Live interruption/truncated recovery remains unverified. Supported groups_dirty scheduling and ACK are implemented offline; other unsolicited group notifications remain unsupported. Batch group-refresh replies now use their supported mixed-union path: full results commit beside exact truncated=true/size=0..19999 and group@error=403/404 items, with a durable projection report. These size/error items preserve old membership instead of failing the whole supported batch. Invalid/unrecognized or uncorrelated items still preserve the whole prior state. group refresh --follow-up enables bounded supported-result continuation; group refresh-status --id reports counts, round, next_action, pending and exhaustion; absent reports remain distinguishable only by inspecting action state. Direct single-group truncated snapshot ingestion retains its earlier explicit refusal behavior. Mixed/report behavior is offline tested, not live verified. Supported authenticated w:gp2/groups_dirty notifications now atomically queue one zero-estimate truncatable group refresh plus a durable from/ID-scoped deduplication marker before returning the notification ACK. ACK fields are to/id/class/type and optional participant; recipient/category/edit are not echoed. Duplicate supported inputs may repeat the ACK but never create or resend a query; same from/ID with changed supported inputs refuses without ACK. Local limits: one root child, 1..256 listed group nodes, concrete unique non-device group JIDs, nonempty ID <=128 bytes and parseable from/participant. Missing jid nodes are skipped as in APK 37.71 0yv.A09; an empty remaining list is unacknowledged rather than creating the APK job that later throws. Unsupported shapes stay captured and log secret-free diagnostics; storage failure stops receiving. Existing actions lists the refresh dirty groups intent; group refresh-status inspects its eventual bounded projection chain. Queueing also occurs without --send-outbox, since this is a protocol read. Offline injected-link ACK-write-cut and encrypted-store reopen/deduplication tests cover durability; Live 2026-10-07: a bounded 45-second saved-account receive session (zero queued actions/chat intents at preflight) observed two w:gp2 notification log lines, queued one refresh dirty groups action, settled it ok with one complete group projected in-session and no pending/truncated/follow-up inputs, then stopped cleanly. Notification ACK socket writing completed without session error, but no separate server confirmation of that ACK is claimed. The unresolved two-factor action stayed sent and no incoming user message was logged. Live truncated continuation, conflicting/duplicate dirty inputs and notification failure recovery remain unverified. Other group notification types and APK error/wait helpers remain unfinished.

post.summary: Compute native fingerprint display from explicit inputs (offline)
post.description: CLI only; no HTTP route. Does not open the account store, fetch keys, compare QR data, select the active APK scheme, or commit human verification. Reads a private regular JSON file <=64 KiB with local/remote sides (FingerprintDisplayInput). Rejects unknown fields; error text omits offending values. Raw keys are sorted unsigned, serialized with 0x05, concatenated without deduplication and hashed using APK 37.71 native 5200-round identifier-bound SHA-512. Six big-endian five-byte groups yield 30 digits per side, with lexical join to 60. Native-display fixtures use actual ARM64 hash control flow with host-modeled SHA/MCF; whole native display and live comparison are not established. Complete device inventory and scheme selection remain caller responsibilities. Output contains no input identifier or public key. Resource bounds are client policy. See docs/protocol/safety-number.md. Optional --qr-version 0|1 plus --qr-output exports APK-derived native V4 combined fingerprint protobuf to a new private mode-600 binary file, without opening account storage. V4 QR needs full plain-primary lid_jid matching display_identifier and at least PN or username presence on each side. Optional QR-specific fields are ignored for display-only calculations. V4 local PN is suppressed with a present username; remote PN retained. Version 1 uses H(K,K), not identifier-bound display hash. Full identifiers and key/hash material appear in the private export, never stdout. Refuses existing output or invalid inputs before export; partial write failures preserve the private artifact. No QR image rendering, scan, peer comparison, active scheme/inventory assertion or verification commit. Independent literal-tag wire fixtures use host-modeled-SHA actual ARM64 hash flow for digests; full native serialization and live scan remain unverified. Explicit --qr-scheme native-v3 selects V3 binary export (omitting it preserves native-v4). This flag requires qr-version/qr-output. V3 retains both PN fields despite username presence; optional LID supports the traced numeric-primary subset and zero-device suffixes, whose supplied full text is retained. V3 display/export requires pn_identifier equal to display_identifier on each side: a conservative CLI subset based on native stable-PN display, not a server rule. Library encode_v3 also supports LID-only explicit inputs without displaying. Independent V3 literal-wire fixtures cover versions 0/1, both addresses, PN-only, LID-only, zero suffix, optional presence and export/compare orientation. Static native serializer trace confirms fields/order; full native pack/JNI/current inventory and live scanning remain unverified.

post.summary: Compare native V3/V4 binary payload with explicit known inputs (offline)
post.description: CLI only; no HTTP route. Same private JSON format as fingerprint-display plus a private scanned binary protobuf file. Both regular files <=64 KiB and exclude group/other permissions. Does not open an account store, select current scheme/inventory, fetch keys, render/decode a QR image, send or commit human verification. Implements APK 2.26.37.71 conversion/presence order, LID-directed orientation, version-selected key comparison, PN equality, ASCII username equality with exact length and hosted-state legacy branch. Local-first native results are remapped; remote-first are direct. Known params retain both PN/username (no local QR serializer suppression). Native internal codes are surfaced without invented UI/server meanings. Empty/oversized payload refuses as our local resource policy instead of the APK empty-buffer abort. ASCII username equality is independently validated using actual APK merged MCFStringCompare and the pinned public Bionic fixture; other Android implementations remain unverified. Bounded native fingerprint-schema parsing replaces prost after eight acceptance differences were observed. Actual 50-case unpack/free corpus covers accepted/decoded fields, duplicates, unknown enums/fields, groups, wire types, varints and length boundaries. Five-byte tags/lengths, ten-byte scalar termination (low32 values), first-byte tag guard, int31 length bound and message merge follow native rules. Groups refuse even beside otherwise matching data, correcting a possible false match. Other edges remain unverified and reported; opaque unknown data is skipped, not round-tripped. Known CLI inputs require ordinary canonical primary LIDs matching display_identifier and PN/username presence; these existing operator guards are not inferred server requirements. Output has no identifiers, keys or payload. Synthetic fixtures and all 113 executed non-abort core cases plus 268 native string cases test semantics. No live peer scan or current input selection is established. See docs/protocol/safety-number.md. Explicit --scheme native-v3 enables APK V3 conversion/orientation/core/remapping; default native-v4 preserves existing behavior. V3 allows PN-only or LID-only known sides and does not require PN/username presence together. Username equality is case-sensitive bytes; orientation and remote identity accept PN OR normalized primary LID. Local/remote PN omission statuses differ; full native subset documented in docs/protocol/safety-number.md. --v3-hosted enables options 3; without it V3 uses options 1 (username checks always). This is operator selection, not inferred APK flags. The flag refuses with native-v4. Same JSON format is reused; V3 display_identifier is present for format compatibility but unused by comparison. V3 adds scheme/options/lid_parser_authority output; modeled native branch corpus and remaining MCF/JNI/input-selection unknowns are explicit. V3 comparison does not export a payload or commit verification; V3 export is separately available through fingerprint-display --qr-scheme native-v3.

post.summary: Queue one classic batch group refresh
post.description: Offline queueing of one APK 37.71 classic w:g2 IQ to g.us with query context per_group_dirty_recovery and group children carrying jid. Repeat --chat for each concrete distinct group (local bound one to 256). Correlated mixed groups/group results now atomically commit full snapshots/events and a durable projection outcome. Exact group@error=403/404 count as forbidden/not_found without deleting previous snapshots. Exact truncated=true requires explicit size 0..19999 and stores pending JID/size without replacing membership. Missing/extra/duplicate/unexpected identities, unknown errors, child-error shapes or invalid truncated sizes preserve the whole prior state and saved response. Inspect projection counts using group refresh-status --id; action IQ status alone is not complete refresh success. The earlier two-full-group batch was live verified; mixed/report behavior is offline tested only. Default queueing has no follow-up. --follow-up opts into per_group_dirty_recovery_truncatable with initial zero estimates and APK-derived maximum round 2 (at most two further queries). Supported truncated results and unsent partitions create distinct queries atomically with projection; original input order is preserved. Conservative local participant budget 10000 selects only the first partition per round; current APK heap/feature cap is unknown. Full and 403/404 groups are excluded from continuation. Refused, uncertain, unanswered or unsupported results never generate a next query. Reports expose round, next_action, pending count and exhausted. No notification ACK is queued. Root refusals retain the action queue behavior. Supported automatic groups_dirty scheduling/ACK now uses this bounded truncatable pipeline in listen; offline tested only. Other notifications, full union metadata, MEX and APK wait handling remain unfinished. CLI-only; no HTTP route exists. Complete full-group snapshots now preserve group_type and linked_parent. APK 37.71 ADs.A01 checks child presence with precedence parent, default_sub_group, general_chat, linked_parent, otherwise ordinary. Text/attributes do not affect classification. ADs.A03 extracts linked_parent@jid; only supported concrete non-device group identities are stored. Historical rows/local stubs default both new fields to null without rewriting or guessing ordinary. group list --json exposes these fields; metadata-only changes do not add new event types. Direct and batch full-reply paths share parsing. Subject notification application/alias mapping remain unfinished and classification is offline tested, not live validated. Observed live 2026-10-07: one bounded 30-second saved-account receive session transmitted one newly queued existing-group info query, settled it ok and projected ordinary classification/null parent for four members. The unqueried historical snapshot remained null; zero queued actions/chat intents remained, and an unresolved two-factor action stayed sent. Other type branches and subject notification application remain live unverified. Queue/list commands themselves are offline; no HTTP route added.

get.summary: Inspect one saved batch projection outcome
get.description: Offline counts-only inspection of the encrypted RefreshOutcome for an existing group-refresh action ID. Prints complete, truncated, forbidden, not_found counts, automatic_follow_up, round, next_action (or null), pending count and exhausted. JSON null means no report is saved; inspect actions for pending/refused/unapplied state or a historical completed batch. Does not queue a query, backfill old markers, print group IDs/sizes or claim every group is refreshed. Per-group 403/404 preserve snapshots; size-only groups remain pending; opt-in chains can stop at round 2 with exhausted=true. Inspect next_action separately for its own outcome. Historical reports lacking continuation metadata default to no automatic continuation. Mixed/outcome and continuation behavior is offline tested, not live verified. CLI-only; no HTTP route exists.
